focus.label: Peripheral vestibulocochlear disorder due to fat-containing lesion (likely lipoma) at the porus acusticus
focus.why: The current frontier 'Vestibular/peripheral disorder' is too broad. MRI directly shows a fat-containing lesion at the porus acusticus (node-6), and the porus acusticus is the entry point of the vestibulocochlear nerve (node-9). This anatomical and imaging evidence strongly supports a fat-containing tumor such as a lipoma compressing the nerve, refining the frontier to a specific peripheral lesion.

payload.query: Need fat-suppressed MRI and high-resolution heavily T2-weighted cisternography (CISS/FIESTA) of the internal auditory canal to confirm the lesion is fat and to delineate its exact relation to the vestibulocochlear nerve at the porus acusticus; this is critical for validating the suspected lipoma and differentiating it from schwannoma or meningioma, thereby strengthening the peripheral vestibulocochlear disorder and limiting residual central uncertainty.
